 Order
With the consent of the parties, matter is heard finally at motion hearing stage.

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved with the award passed by I st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shahdol,
District Shahdol (M.P.) in Claim Case MVC No.9/2014 vide order dated 18.12.2015 by which the claim petition was allowed and the claimants were awarded Rs.5,55,000/- compensation with @9%
interest per annum.
2.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellants has submitted that though she has filed the appeal for enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/- as the Trial Court has wrongly assessed the monthly income of the deceased and has not awarded any amount on the head of future prospect but she is not pressing the appeal except this, on other grounds.
3. Learned counsel for appellant has submitted that as per the judgment of Apex Court, the deceased-person may be self-employment or any other is entitled for future prospect.

In this case,
the deceased was of 36 years and income has been decided Rs.3,000/- per month.

Hence, the 50%
amount of monthly income be added in the amount of future prospect in the multiplier of 15 be maintained and she is not pressing other grounds.
4. Learned counsel for Insurance Company has submitted that the appeal was filed by 552 days of delay and for that period, no interest be awarded and the order of pay and recover be maintained.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the parties.
6. Perused the record.

7. In this case, the Claims Tribunal while deciding the issue no.6 has assessed the monthly income of the decease Rs.3,000/- and on that basis, annual income of the deceased is Rs.36,000/- but the Trial Court has not awarded any income in the head of future prospect.

The Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, AIR 2017 SC 5157 has laid down the principle where the deceased is self- employed or working on the fixed salary, if he is below the 40 years age then 40% of income shall be added in the future prospect and this principle was following in the case of Hansraj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd, 2018 ACJ 5 SC.

sentences.text: In the subsequent judgments on that basis, the claimants are entitled for amount on the head of future prospect @40% of the established income on that basis, the Trial Court has applied the multiplier of 15 as per the judgment of Mrs. Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, 2009 ACJ 1298 SC.

sentences.text:
On that basis if the calculation is done, the loss of dependency comes as under :-
 (a) Annual income 36,000/
 (b) 40% future prospect 14,400/
 (c) Deduction 1/4th 12,600/

(d) Annual loss of dependency 37,800/
 (e) Total loss of dependency = 37,8,00x1  Rs.5,67,
8 .
The Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,05,000/-.
Thus, the compensation amount on the head of loss of dependency is enhanced Rs.1,62,000/-.

9. Claimants are also entitled on the enhancement amount i.e. Rs.1,62,000/- simple interest @9%
from the date of application i.e. 10.02.2014 to 18.12.2015 and from the date of 09.02.2024 till enhanced amount is deposited before the Claims Tribunal on the rest of the grounds the award of Claims Tribunal is affirmed and it is also clarified that the Insurance Company shall be entitled to recover the amount from the owner and driver as directed by Claims Tribunal.
The Claims Tribunal shall disburse the amount in the same ration and on the same terms and conditions as directed in the impugned award.
With the above direction, the appeal is partly allowed.
10. With the copy of this order, the record of the Claims Tribunal be returned back.
11. Record of this appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
